reviewStandard: Current identity and NCBI Taxonomy identifiers were checked against NCBI Taxonomy and LPSN, and morphology was bounded by primary descriptions or referenced type-strain records. One built-in generation call was made for each supported subject using the immutable passive prompt record, followed by one targeted Burkholderiales revision call after root rejected its shared multi-cell outer boundary. The WikiBiome media task inspected every copied PNG at original 1536 by 1024 resolution and reconciled visible bodies and groupings without trusting prompt counts. Root accepted five first-generation drafts and Burkholderiales generation revision 2; generation revision 1 remains rejected review evidence. Only the accepted exact files are eligible for deterministic promotion, subject to the approved review log and every release gate.

revisionLinkage.replacementReason: Root rejected revision 1 because a shared translucent outer boundary around the lower-right three-rod grouping could read as an invented capsule, sheath, microcolony envelope, biofilm, or enclosing membrane. Revision 2 gives every body only its own ordinary boundary.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and LPSN recognize Burkholderiales as current order NCBITaxon:80840. Multiple current families and referenced descendant records support a selected order-level plate spanning straight rods, short oval rods, coccoid forms, and grouped cylindrical rods. The plate is explicitly non-exhaustive, non-diagnostic, uses illustrative relative scale, and asserts no shared envelope or order-diagnostic surface structure.
assets.visualReview: Exactly nine cellular bodies appear in five separated groupings: one touching pair of medium straight rods, one touching pair of small plump oval bodies, one single near-spherical body, one single short rounded rod, and one aligned three-rod grouping with small visible gaps. Each body has only its own ordinary clean boundary; no shared outer envelope, sheath, halo, capsule, biofilm, or enclosing membrane appears. No labels, arrows, scale bar, appendages, spores, host material, scenery, crowding, clipping, or watermark are visible.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and LPSN recognize Campylobacter as current genus NCBITaxon:194. assets.scientificFinding: NCBI Taxonomy and LPSN recognize Campylobacter jejuni as current species NCBITaxon:197. The plate therefore makes no species-diagnostic morphology claim and omits external flagella.
